stages.name: Financial sector failure
stages.title: Financial sector failure
stages.sub: How a bursting bubble spreads harm beyond the financial sector, and how rigged markets fail too.

steps.q: Speculative buyers have pushed the price of an asset far above what it is really worth. Confidence suddenly disappears. What happens to the price?
steps.hint: Everyone who was buying on confidence now wants to sell at once.

steps.q: Banks and investors who borrowed heavily to buy that asset now hold something worth far less. What happens to the financial system around them?
steps.hint: If lenders suddenly can't get their money back, what happens to the whole system of banks and lending?

steps.q: So after the bubble mechanism drives prices up and confidence collapses, what set of effects follows?
steps.right: A sharp crash and a shaky financial system
steps.wrong: A short pause before prices rise again
steps.hint: Think of the collapse and the instability together, as one outcome of the bubble bursting.

steps.q: Struggling banks now lend far less to ordinary businesses and households. Does this stay inside the financial sector, or spread further?
steps.right: It spreads into the wider economy
steps.wrong: It stays inside the financial sector
steps.hint: Businesses that relied on loans to invest and hire, what happens to them now?

steps.q: Firms and households who never bought the asset, and never chose to take on its risk, still lose jobs and loans when it collapses. Are they bearing a cost they agreed to?
steps.right: No, it's a cost imposed on them
steps.wrong: Yes, they knew the risk they were taking
steps.hint: They didn't buy the asset or take the risk themselves, so where did this cost come from?

steps.wrong: Yes, it still reflects genuine trading
steps.hint: They didn't compete separately, they agreed together on what number to submit.
